Title: Orchard PYO Covid
Content: Thank you for considering a visit to Nashoba Valley.     Thanks for planning a visit to Nashoba Valley today for apple picking. We are thrilled that you will be joining us and thankful that you are supporting a local farm. These are very difficult times for the restaurant/tourism business and it is especially difficult for family-owned farms. We appreciate the support that we have received and we thank everyone that appreciates all of the changes that we have been required to institute for the safety of our visitors and staff.     Per guidelines issued by the Commonwealth of Massachusetts: PYO staff and customers must utilize cloth face coverings/masks while harvesting crops at PYO locations in-line with CDC guidance, as well as state and local requirements. This is particularly important for certain PYO crops that place customers in close proximity to fruit being harvested. Customers should be allowed to utilize masks and face coverings that they bring with them to the farm. Customers who do not have masks or cloth face coverings should not be allowed in PYO harvest areas. Everyone's hands should be sanitized before and after picking. Try to only touch the fruit that you are interested in harvesting. Thank you for your cooperation.      Finally, please remember that you need a separate reservation to enter the picnic grounds and alcoholic beverages can only be consumed while seated at a table and after you have order food. Please appreciate that we are fully booked for this weekend and while you can check for cancellation, it is not likely that seating will be available. Again, thank you for your understanding.      Please continue to support local restaurants and farms as it is projected that as many as 85% of independent restaurants may permanently close because of the pandemic by the end of 2020.      For additional information please refer to https://nashobawinery.com/orchard/apples/   No reservations are necessary for apple picking

Title: Vegan Wines
Content:
Nashoba does not use animal by products in the fining of its wines.  Instead we relay on natural settlement, enzymes, cross flow filtration, cold stability, gum arabic (acacia tree) and a clay-based fining agent called bentonite.  Our approach is sufficiently efficient at fining out unwanted proteins so there is no need to use other agents in the process.      Most wines, if left long enough, will self-stabilize and self-fine. However, traditionally producers have used a variety of aids called ‘fining agents’ to help the process along. Fining agents help precipitate out these haze-inducing molecules. Essentially, the fining agent acts like a magnet – attracting the molecules around it. They coagulate around the fining agent, creating fewer but larger particles, which can then be more easily removed.     The reason that all wines are not vegan or even vegetarian-friendly has to do with how the wine is clarified and a process called ‘fining’. All young wines are hazy and contain tiny molecules such as proteins, tartrates, tannins and phenolics. These are all natural, and in no way harmful. However, we wine-drinkers like our wines to be clear and bright.      
 Traditionally the most commonly used fining agents were casein (a milk protein), albumin (egg whites), gelatin (animal protein) and isinglass (fish bladder protein). These fining agents are known as processing aids. They are not additives to the wine, as they are precipitated out along with the haze molecules.     
 Fining with casein and albumin is usually acceptable by most vegetarians but all four are off limits for vegans because tiny traces of the fining agent may be absorbed into the wine during the fining process.   Because Nashoba simply does not use animal based fining agents, our wines are vegan friendly.

Title: Event Planning 2023
Content: Thank you for thinking of Nashoba Valley Winery for your event.  For 2023, we have decided to limit the number of private events/functions that we host so that we can focus on our daily operations.  We apologize that we are unable to be more creative and flexible with our event offerings at this time but for the hospitality industry, the staff is the most important component for successful operations.  Currently,  we simply cannot hire enough staff to host as many events and functions as we previously hosted or to take on more complicated events such as large weddings.     Currently, we are only booking events for 2023 and not booking events or reserving dates for 2024 and beyond. Here is what we are currently offering.  Exclusive Restaurant Experience  Since we have been able to retain our staff at J's Restaurant we continue offering our "Exclusive Restaurant Experience" for private gatherings.   The Restaurant is a great location for gatherings of 25 to 50 people with the entire first floor and outside areas reserved exclusively for your guests.  You will be served and accommodated by the restaurant staff that has remained loyal to us throughout the past years.  This event is perfect for an eloquent small wedding, birthday celebration, shower or anniversary where you want to present a fine dining experience in our rustic restaurant.  To learn more about this experience and to reach out to a function coordinator, please Click Here for Information on our Exclusive Restaurant Experience.  After reviewing the information on the link, please fill out the form on the suggested link page to discuss additional information or dates.   Our Distillery Lunch Buffet  Our Distillery is available on Saturday and Sunday during the day for 15 to 40 people.   The area is about 20 X 45 surrounded by Stills, columns, and thumpers!  Events are hosted for 3 hours with an additional hour at the beginning of the event should you need to set up or decorate.   We have priced this hosted event at $58.50 per person which includes, rental, tables, chairs,  and food. (tip 19% and tax 7% not included).   For additional information, click here https://nashobawinery.com/dspevent/  This area is not available on weekdays since the area is part of our production operations so our team will be busy making great spirits for you to enjoy at home.   Outdoor Patio Experience  We are opening our Outdoor covered patio area for Corporate Outings and Celebrations Outside during the day on Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday from 11 am until 5 pm.  The patio area can accommodate  25 to 45 people.   Events are hosted for 3 hours with an additional hour at the beginning of the event should you need to set up or decorate.   We have priced this hosted event at $42.75 per person which includes, rental, tables, chairs, food, and soft drinks(tip 19% and tax 7% not included).    For additional information, click here https://nashobawinery.com/outevents/  This event is not available on Saturdays or Sundays.  Thanks for your understanding, your support, and your appreciation of family-owned farms and local businesses.

Title: Weather Questions
Content:
From our website 
 
 Vintners Knoll - Reservations 
 If, in our opinion, we do not feel that it is reasonable to expect our customers to sit outdoors as a result of the weather, we will notify all customers, at least 3 hours before their reservation time, of our decision to offer refunds for the fee paid but not the processing fee charged by Fareharbor (usually about $1.00). 
 To receive a refund, customers must respond that they wish to cancel prior to the time of their reservation.  If we do not receive a response, we will hold the reservation for you and will assume that you will be attending.  If we receive a response indicating that you wish to cancel prior to the time for your arrival, we will issue the refunds within 48 hours. 
 However, it is important to note that the decision to cancel is at our discretion as we have experience in several situations where actual weather is much different than predicted weather.  If you decide in advance of our notice to cancel, we will not issue a refund.  We never shut down due to weather (excepting extreme weather such as hurricanes, blizzards, or flooding) so you are always invited to visit.  If you received a notice that we are accepting cancellations, please email support@nashobawinery.com if you have elected not to visit as a result of the weather. 
   
 Vintners Knoll - Food 
 Please refrain from ordering food until you have are sure that you will be honoring your reservation and until you are confident that the weather will cooperate.  Food is perishable so once we begin our preparation for the day, it is too late.  If you order food and wine and decide not to visit, the order cannot be canceled but will be made available for curbside pickup if you notify us.  It is your decision when to order food as food can be ordered at any time including in advance of your reservation or once you arrive.

Title: Shipping out of State
Content:
First and foremost, please accept our apology for not being able to ship to you at this time.  We are working on it and hope to be able to ship to some of the “Strategic” states in the near future. 
 
 
 
        
 
       
 
Unfortunately, shipping of alcoholic beverages between states in the United States is very complicated.  To ship wine to any state, a winery is required, at a minimum, to obtain a Direct To Consumer (DTC) permit from the state that it intends to ship wine into.  Direct-to-Consumer (DTC) alcohol shipping is governed by individual state regulations, and any person or business looking to legally ship wine needs a DTC license. For most alcohol retailers, the license is covered by their off-premise wine sales licenses.  Some states are expensive while others are not.   Once you are over the hurdle of applying for a DTC permit, you will also need to register with the tax authority for the state so that you are able to pay for state and local taxes associated with each shipment.   Most states require monthly reports to the Alcohol Commission for the state informing them of your shipments the person ship to as well as the amount.  Additionally, most states require monthly reports and payments to the taxing authority and many require additional annual reports.  If you are registered to sell into all 50 states, you can probably be expecting to file over a thousand reports per month.
 
 At one time Nashoba was registered in 26 states and the experience cost us about $15,000 as sales did not cover the costs of permits and compliance.  Some states carry heavy administrative burdens, some less so and we did not prepare for all of the burdens associated with each state. Participating in the DTC segment of the wine market requires a strategy that we did not have previously.

Unfortunately, shipping of alcoholic beverages between states in the United States is very complicated.  To ship wine to any state, a winery is required, at a minimum, to obtain a Direct To Consumer (DTC) permit from the state that it intends to ship wine into.  Direct-to-Consumer (DTC) alcohol shipping is governed by individual state regulations, and any person or business looking to legally ship wine needs a DTC license. For most alcohol retailers, the license is covered by their off-premise wine sales licenses.  Some states are expensive while others are not.   Once you are over the hurdle of applying for a DTC permit, you will also need to register with the tax authority for the state so that you are able to pay for state and local taxes associated with each shipment.   Most states require monthly reports to the Alcohol Commission for the state informing them of your shipments the person ship to as well as the amount.  Additionally, most states require monthly reports and payments to the taxing authority and many require additional annual reports.  If you are registered to sell into all 50 states, you can probably be expecting to file over a thousand reports per month.

Title: Weather and the Vintner's Knoll
Content: You can never count on or predict the weather in New England.  We encourage people to wait until they are comfortable that the weather will cooperate to book a reservation although we admit that this is difficult in New England.   When you book a reservation that is not refundable, you are accepting the risk that the weather may not be perfect or meet your expectations.  Too often the prediction for rain does not materialize or a nice day turns into a rainy day.  All reservations are non-refundable and we do not have alternative inside seating.  If on the date of your reservation, and not prior to the date, we feel that it is not reasonable for people to sit outside then in our discretion, we may decide to allow people to re-schedule or to elect a tasting or tour as an alternative sometimes requiring additional fees.   This decision is solely at our discretion.  The decision will be made on the actual date of the reservation based on the actual weather and not the forecast.  If we decide to offer alternative plans, it may take up to 48 hours to complete the transaction.  Thank you for your understanding and lets wait to see what the weather brings.

Title: Tastings & Dinner
Content: Unfortunately  we do not have packages so you will have to make two separate reservations.       I would suggest that book a reservation for dinner at J's first to insure availability and then book a reservation for you tasting 75 minutes before the time you select to dine with us.  The last tasting that we offer on Saturday is at 5:15 so you would want a reservation at 6:30 pm.   Alternatively, the first reservation that we take at J's is at 5:00 pm so if this time is selected, I would book a tasting at 3:45 pm.      We offer tastings on weekends in two separate areas.  One is a casual location where we offer tastings in a stand up environment.  This area is referred to as the Pavilion.  Information about the Pavilion Tastings can be found by clicking here.      Alternatively, we offer a more formal tasting area in the winery, which also offers small plates although I would suggest waiting for J's food if you are looking for inspiration.  Information on our Winery Tasting Area can be found by clicking here.   Having food at the Winery Tasting Area is optional.     There are separate entrances an parking lots to the restaurant and winery but both are in close walking distance to both buildings.  However, even though you are going tot he winery first,  please park at the restaurant as that parking area is closest to your final destination and is lighted.     Thanks and sorry that our system does not have a bundling feature.       The Nashoba Team.
